title: Localized PD-1 CAR T therapy reprograms neuroinflammation.
journal: Cell 189(18), Sep 2026 (PMID 42480527). Europe PMC: isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, 'Subscription required' — no full text available, and no preprint found in Europe PMC. Only the abstract was readable. Senior affiliation: Dept of Systems Immunology, Weizmann Institute.
data_url: GEO SuperSeries GSE327497 = GSE308973 (human CSF, 88 samples) + GSE327494 (mouse CAR T, 302 samples). FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE308nnn/GSE308973/suppl/ and .../GSE327nnn/GSE327494/suppl/

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both annotation tables and 9 per-plate count matrices. GSE308973_SPID_metadata_annotated_new.txt.gz (427 KB): 33,792 rows x 14 cols; 18 patients, tissue='csf' only, 8 diagnoses (RRMS 9 patients, PPMS 2, Active PPMS 1, CIS 2, plus 4 non-MS), 3 categories (MS 14 / CNS inflammatory 2 / Peripheral inflammatory 2), 5 batches, 88 Amp_batch_IDs x exactly 384 wells, 'clusters' blank for 19,078 of 33,792 cells (16 named cell types for the remaining 14,714). GSE327494_adata_obs_for_GEO.csv.gz (389 KB): 92,468 rows x 10 cols; 64 mouse IDs, 78 unique (mouse,batch), 5 tissues, 12 batches, 28 cell types, treatment in {Untreated(PBS) 57,602 cells, aPD-1 CAR 16,995, aPD-1 CAR+IL-10 8,953, control 5,000, IL-10 3,918}, score in {0,0.5,1,1.5,2.5,3,'control'}, 2 EAE models, 2 protocols (SPID/MARS). Count matrices: genes x 384 wells, integer UMIs, gene symbols as row names (human 57,874 genes; mouse 52,634). Human join verified exact: all 384 wells of GSM9257593_AB11353 are in the metadata. Mouse join partially broken: 5 of 8 plates I checked use 'WMC...' well IDs with 0/384 overlap with the obs table (and stripping 'MC' also gives 0 matches); the 3 'W...' plates overlap 187, 340, 322 of 384. GSM-level characteristics confirmed to carry tissue/patient/diagnosis/category (human) and tissue/mouse/score/treatment/eae model/batch/gate (mouse).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology and the CAR T experiments comes from the 120-word abstract plus the GEO series summary: the PD-1+ Tfh-like subset, TCR restriction, IgG+ B cell/plasma cell enrichment, IL-10 release, and clinical improvement. No cell counts, patient counts, QC thresholds or figure numbers from the paper could be checked — the Cell article is paywalled and not in PMC. The abstract claims an atlas of CSF, brain and blood, but the deposited human series contains CSF only (tissue column has a single value); brain/blood human data are not in GSE327497. No TCR/VDJ data is deposited in either subseries. NCBI elink PubMed->GEO/SRA/BioProject returned nothing (the GEO link is not yet indexed); the series were found by GEO keyword search. Zenodo and Figshare searches returned nothing.

a1_downloadable.note: Pass (checked). Both series are public on GEO FTP with no login; I downloaded 11 files (HTTP 200, byte sizes matched filelist.txt). Totals: GSE308973_RAW.tar 49.8 MB, GSE327494_RAW.tar 260.9 MB (per-sample txt.gz are 0.4-1.3 MB each, so the cap is avoidable).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Pass only for the coarse labels: diagnosis/category (human) and score/treatment/model/tissue (mouse) are columns in the metadata and in every GSM's characteristics. The paper's actual finding — the rare activated PD-1+ TCR-restricted Tfh-like subset — is NOT a column: the 16 human cluster names contain no Tfh/PD-1 category, and no TCR data is deposited, so that target would have to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Pass (checked). Real UMI count matrices with gene symbols are present, not accessions — 390 plate files, ~310 MB gzipped total, each 384 wells. Cost: 390 downloads plus a gene-symbol union concatenation.

a4_units_stated.note: Weak pass. Expression is integer UMI counts, stated in Sample_data_processing ('mRNA molecule count values'); no normalization is shipped. The mouse 'score' column has no stated scale and mixes the string 'control' into an otherwise numeric 0-3 EAE scale.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL (checked). The independent unit is the patient or the animal: 18 human patients (14 MS, 2 CNS-inflammatory, 2 peripheral-inflammatory; cells per patient 384-3,840) and 64 mice / 78 (mouse,batch) samples across 5 treatment arms. 33,792 and 92,468 cells look large but are nested; this is the scCT-DB failure mode from the checklist's worked examples. Under 400 even for pure classification, and the non-MS comparison group is 4 patients.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~310 MB gzipped raw; ~126k cells x ~50k genes sparse is roughly 1-3 GB in memory depending on filtering. Annotation tables are under 1 MB.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Pass for a laptop in sparse form. Backbone embedding of 126k cells on CPU would take many hours but is a one-time cacheable cost.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: FAIL as 'cannot be reconciled'. Human side is exact (88 x 384 = 33,792 rows, 384/384 wells join). Mouse side does not reconcile: the obs table has 92,468 cells while 302 plates x 384 = 115,968 wells are deposited, and the plates using 'WMC' well IDs (5 of 8 I sampled) have zero ID overlap with the obs table in either direction, so for those plates there is no way to tell which cells the released annotations refer to. The paper itself is paywalled, so no stated count could be compared.

a8_label_provenance.note: Split verdict. The low-n labels are clean physical/clinical measurements: diagnosis is from the clinic, treatment arm is experimentally assigned, EAE score is a behavioural readout — all independent of transcriptome. But the only high-n label, cell_type / clusters, was produced by Seurat scaling-PCA-clustering plus marker annotation of the very count matrix that would be the input (stated in Sample_data_processing). That is label-computed-from-features, so within-dataset cell-type prediction is circular.

existing_models.name: Human CSF single-cell compendium (Ostkamp et al., J Clin Invest 2025, PMC11684814) — 'A single-cell compendium of human cerebrospinal fluid identifies disease-associated immune cell populations'
existing_models.score_and_split: Not read (abstract-level retrieval only); it is a reference/atlas resource rather than a released predictor, and it aggregates far more donors than the 18 patients here.

existing_models.name: Schafflick et al., Nat Commun 2020 (PMC6959356) — integrated single-cell analysis of blood and CSF leukocytes in MS
existing_models.score_and_split: Descriptive atlas, no published predictor or split. Relevant as the long-standing public MS CSF reference rather than as a model.

existing_models.name: scGPT / Geneformer / scFoundation as cell-type annotators
existing_models.score_and_split: Zero-shot benchmarking (Genome Biology 2025, 10.1186/s13059-025-03574-x, retrieved via search summary) reports that scGPT and Geneformer are outperformed by highly-variable-gene selection plus Harmony/scVI on cell-type clustering BIO score; BioLLM (Patterns 2025) provides a standardized fine-tuning/zero-shot annotation harness.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Reliability in the zero-shot regime where labels are unknown; whether the models beat simple HVG baselines at all.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (human and mouse scRNA-seq UMI counts, gene symbols present, so no ID mapping needed)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU; embedding ~126k cells is an overnight one-time cost, cacheable. No GPU needed for a linear/MLP head.
backbone.licence: Not verified this session for either backbone. GEO deposits carry no explicit data licence; the Cell article is subscription-only, so figures/text cannot be redistributed.

integration.partner_dataset: Would have been the human CSF compendium (J Clin Invest 2025, PMC11684814) or Schafflick 2020 (Nat Commun) as an independent CSF reference; mouse side has no natural large partner beyond public EAE scRNA-seq.
integration.join_key: HGNC gene symbol at the feature level and cell-type label name at the annotation level — there is no shared sample or subject key.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a CSF immune-cell annotator trained on large public CSF compendia transfer to a plate-based (MARS/SPID) MS CSF cohort and to CAR-T-treated mouse CNS, or does it collapse across platform and species? — a fair question, but it cannot be answered here because the only labels available at scale are themselves clustering output (A8) and the cohort is 18 patients (A5).

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: recover canonical marker separation (CD3D/CD8A/MS4A1/CD14) and predict total UMI count from the matrix as a plumbing check.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle cell-type labels within plate; shuffle patient labels within batch — essential here because 5 human batches partly track diagnosis.
controls.external_validation: Public CSF scRNA-seq (Schafflick 2020, CSF compendium 2025) exists as a second source, so E7 would have scored well had Part A passed. No publication-year column within the deposit.

honest_claim_h3: Among 384-well plate-sorted CSF cells from 18 patients at one Israeli centre (14 of them MS, 4 non-MS controls) and 64 EAE mice from one lab, a model could at best claim to reproduce this lab's own Seurat cluster assignments; it could claim nothing about MS diagnosis, about the PD-1+ Tfh-like subset, or about CAR T response, because those labels exist for 18 and 78 independent units respectively.
ml_idea: The only non-circular, adequately powered task would be cross-cohort cell-type annotation transfer (train on a large public CSF compendium, test here, then mouse), using frozen scGPT/Geneformer embeddings plus a linear head and reporting per-cell-type recall under plate-level grouping. Not worth starting: the labels are clustering output, the mouse annotation table does not join to ~61 of 302 plates, and open annotators plus an honest zero-shot benchmark already exist.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count independent units before anything else: `18 patients, 4 of them non-MS` and `64 mice / 78 (mouse,batch) samples` — done in 5 minutes from the two 400 KB metadata files, and it kills every patient- or animal-level label. Second check, also cheap: intersect each mouse plate's well IDs with GSE327494_adata_obs_for_GEO.csv.gz; 'WMC'-prefixed plates return zero matches.

verdict_reason: Part A fails three ways, all verified in the files. A5: the independent unit is 18 patients (only 4 non-MS) and 64 mice, so every clinically interesting label — diagnosis, treatment arm, EAE score — is hopelessly underpowered despite 126k cells. A8: the only high-n label, cell_type, is Seurat clustering output on the same count matrix, i.e. computed from the features. A7: ~61 of 302 mouse plates use 'WMC' well IDs that have zero overlap with the released annotation table, so those cells cannot be matched to any label. The paper is also paywalled with no PMC or preprint full text, the deposited human data is CSF only (no brain or blood despite the abstract), and no TCR data is deposited, so the headline PD-1+ Tfh-like population cannot even be reconstructed.
